newsitem.title: USA: Conoco says LA refinery running, but fire hurts 3.
newsitem.headline: Conoco says LA refinery running, but fire hurts 3.

text.p: Conoco Inc, a wholly-owned unit of Dupont Co, said on Tuesday that a fire Monday at its refinery in Lake Charles, La., injured three employees but had no effect on the unit's operations.
"The bottom line is that we have no units down (at the 180,000 barrel per day (bpd) refinery)," said Leslie Beckhoff, a Conoco spokeswoman.
"We had no output impact," as a result of the fire, she said.
Beckhoff explained that at around 1800 EDT/2200 GMT on Monday, a flash fire occurred in the vapor recovery unit while workers were preparing equipment for scheduled maintenance.
She said the fire, which lasted only "about three seconds," burned three Conoco employees. They were eventually transported to a burn unit in Baton Rouge, Louisiana.

U.S. Gulf Coast spot products traders said gasoline differentials had firmed during the session, but it was not immediately clear whether Conoco was involved in spot market purchases due to the incident.
-- Franklin Paul, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
